newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse correction seen temporary.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse correction seen temporary.

text.p: Belgian shares fell three quarters of a percent in early trading on Thursday, following the Dow's 120-point fall overnight, but dealers said the correction would be short-lived as savers had little alternative to equity investments.
"Who wants to lock in his money in bonds at rates of five to six percent? A lot of cash from bonds maturing goes straight into stocks," one head trader at a Belgian brokerage said.
The Bel-20 index was down 18.98 points or 0.73 pct at 2481.85 in fairly active trade, in line with neighbouring markets.
Dealers noted that trade remained exceptionally active this summer, a period when traditionally many investors stay out of the market.

Trade in shares of non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere (UM) was heavy, with volume of 270,000 shares exchanged, in the aftermath of the sale on Wednesday of 24 percent of the group's capital to institutional investors.
One dealer attributed the volume to investors who did not get their share in yesterday's placement. "UM is one of Belgium's best-known shares, foreign players want it in their portfolios," he said.
Shipper CMB, upgraded from sell to hold by Generale Bank, was down 10 francs at 2590 francs.
Several blue chip shares were down around 1.5 percent, including Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB), which sold the UM stake.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
